scores.evidence: Keyword search matters because users type exact UI labels and error codes, which pure vector search often misses.
scores.rationale: Hybrid pgvector+tsvector with RRF, outbox idempotency, and deletion guard are accurate; minor issues (regex masking before LLM, lightweight phrase scan, Zendesk external-ID details) have little design consequence.

scores.evidence: Non-goals (v1): Account-specific questions ... Actions such as refunds, cancellations or plan changes. Logged-in in-app chat.
scores.rationale: Solves the stated problem, resolves ambiguities with defaults, has explicit justified exclusions and a buildable scope for a 2-person team.

scores.evidence: Each component has 'Owns (single writer)'; Eval Harness imports the same orchestrator code, so evaluation results describe what production actually runs.
scores.rationale: Consistent single-writer ownership; small loose ends such as Chat API enqueue vs Handoff Adapter ownership of outbox, and 'condense on every turn' vs ≤2 calls budget are fine.

scores.evidence: Release blocks if: correctness < 90%, unsupported-claim rate > 2%, escalation recall < 90%, any adversarial violation, retrieval recall@5 drops > 3 points
scores.rationale: Eval set first, judge calibration, spikes early, CI gates, synthetic freshness test, holdout deflection, and production sampling; thresholds are labeled [A] provisional.

scores.evidence: Every default is marked [A] and collected in §5.
scores.rationale: Assumptions table with impact-if-wrong and validation timing; open questions with defaults; numbers labeled estimates.

scores.evidence: a partial sync must never mass-delete the index ... If a run would delete more than 10% of articles, it stops and alerts
scores.rationale: Covers partial sync, duplicate tickets via idempotency, LLM outage degraded mode, stream breaks, injection, cost abuse, restricted-content leakage, XSS, with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Runbooks written in M3: LLM provider outage; 'The bot said something wrong' ... Kill switch
scores.rationale: Alerts on meaningful signals, kill switch, rollback paths, migrations, ownership, business-hours on-call sized to a small team.

scores.evidence: Per turn: ~5k input + 400 output tokens on a mid-tier model ... ≈ $0.02 per turn
scores.rationale: Dominant driver identified with basis, caps and controls, build-vs-buy cost; estimate labeled rough but people cost is thin and the $0.10 vs $0.03 budgets are slightly inconsistent.

scores.evidence: Decision table with Reversibility column; 'Changing the embedding model: insert new rows ... switch Retriever ... through a config flag'
scores.rationale: Reversibility is explicit per decision, with interface isolation, blue/green re-index, build-vs-buy gate before heavy commitment.

scores.evidence: D3. Fixed pipeline, one generation call, no tools or agents ... D4. No RAG framework
scores.rationale: Simplest workable design, single DB, one image, deferred items with triggers; the holdout and backup detail are justified.

scores.evidence: T7→T8→T9→T10 in order; T11 in parallel ... Done when `alembic upgrade head` and `downgrade base` both succeed in CI
scores.rationale: Concrete tasks with locations, checkable done criteria, dependency-based ordering, spikes with plan-changing outcomes.

checklist.evidence: Edited articles show up in answers within 30 min. Unpublished or deleted articles are removed within 30 min
Splits into chunks at H2/H3 headings with a ~600-token cap, prefixing each chunk with `title > heading path`.
Draft evaluation set v1 with the SME: 150 answerable questions (expected article IDs + 1–3 key facts each)
If the best fused score is below a threshold tuned on the evaluation set, skip generation. Return `cannot_answer`
Refunds and billing disputes, account deletion or recovery, legal and privacy requests, security incidents, complaints about staff
The bot has no tools or permissions. Sources and user text are delimited and marked as data.
Keeps only articles that are published, in English, and visible to anonymous users... stops internal or agent-only content from leaking.
Regex masking before storage and before the LLM call. Vendor zero-retention/no-training terms. 90-day retention.
Non-goals (v1): Account-specific questions ("where is my order", "why was I charged").
The support-content team gets a weekly report of "cannot answer" and thumbs-down questions grouped by topic.
Daily spend cap: alert at 80%, at 100% switch automatically to degraded (links-only) mode.

traps.evidence: Answer only from retrieved articles, with checked citations and an explicit "can't answer" path.
Ingest only articles visible to anonymous users. Test: a fixture restricted article must never appear in `documents`.
The `worker` keeps the index in sync with the help center ... scheduled every 15 min
Full suite on prompt, model or orchestrator changes and nightly. Release gate
D3. Fixed pipeline, one generation call, no tools or agents

note: Exceptionally strong, well-scoped plan; main minor weaknesses are the thin people-cost accounting, regex-only PII masking, and lack of per-user entitlements (reasonably out of scope).
